examples: Data governance committee minutes showing compliance monitoring for planning and governance data
Institution-wide planning and governance analytics platform with self-service access

key_discriminator: The institution has moved from comprehensive, governed data management for planning and governance to advanced analytics, predictive capabilities, and recognised sector leadership in data practice

common_false_positives.behaviour: Comprehensive reporting exists for all planning and governance metrics
common_false_positives.why_higher: Complete reporting feels like data excellence
common_false_positives.why_lower: Comprehensive reporting is Integrated. Optimised requires predictive analytics, continuous improvement, and sector contribution beyond descriptive reporting

common_false_positives.behaviour: AI or ML tools are used on planning and governance data
common_false_positives.why_higher: Advanced technology feels like advanced maturity
common_false_positives.why_lower: AI/ML on ungoverned or poor-quality data does not produce Optimised outcomes. The full data quality and governance stack must be mature first

threshold_evidence.minimum: Evidence of advanced analytics or predictive modelling in production use for planning and governance, and contribution to sector data practice
threshold_evidence.strong: Predictive models with documented impact, real-time analytics, exemplary governance referenced by peers, sector contributions through standards or publications, high data literacy enabling self-service advanced analysis
examples: Predictive model for planning and governance with documented improvement in outcomes
Published data governance framework adopted by peer institutions

key_discriminator: The institution has moved from widespread underuse of available digital tools for planning and governance to purposeful promotion of adoption with training, support, and emerging expectations for tool usage

common_false_positives.behaviour: High licence counts exist for planning and governance digital tools
common_false_positives.why_higher: Wide licensing feels like commitment to utilisation
common_false_positives.why_lower: Licence procurement is a Technology decision. Utilisation requires evidence of actual meaningful use of the licensed tools

common_false_positives.behaviour: Some power users achieve impressive results with planning and governance tools
common_false_positives.why_higher: Power user success feels like good utilisation
common_false_positives.why_lower: Individual power users are the Incidental pattern. Intentional requires institutional programmes promoting adoption across the broader user base

threshold_evidence.minimum: Evidence of institutional programmes promoting digital tool adoption for planning and governance with training provision and emerging usage expectations
threshold_evidence.strong: Documented minimum standards for tool usage, training programme with uptake tracking, adoption data for core tools, and management engagement in promoting adoption
examples: Minimum standards document for planning and governance digital tool usage
Training programme schedule with attendance records for planning and governance tools

key_discriminator: The institution has moved from purposeful but uneven promotion of tool adoption for planning and governance to consistent, institution-wide utilisation with monitored standards, impact measurement, and digital workflows replacing manual processes

common_false_positives.behaviour: Most departments report good tool adoption for planning and governance
common_false_positives.why_higher: Widespread self-reported adoption feels like integration
common_false_positives.why_lower: Self-reported adoption without institution-wide monitoring data and consistent standards may mask significant variation. Integration requires verified consistency

common_false_positives.behaviour: Digital workflows exist for some core planning and governance processes
common_false_positives.why_higher: Some digitised processes feel like Integrated utilisation
common_false_positives.why_lower: Selective digitisation alongside persistent manual processes in other areas is Intentional. Integrated requires that digital workflows are the standard for core activities

threshold_evidence.minimum: Evidence of institution-wide adoption monitoring showing consistent utilisation across units, with impact on planning and governance outcomes measured
threshold_evidence.strong: Institution-wide usage dashboards showing consistent high adoption, impact measurement linking tool use to outcomes, user feedback informing optimisation, and digital workflows as standard for core activities
examples: Usage dashboard showing >80% adoption of core planning and governance tool features across all units
Impact analysis linking digital tool utilisation to planning and governance outcome improvements

key_discriminator: The institution has moved from consistent institution-wide utilisation for planning and governance to user-driven innovation, continuous optimisation, and recognised sector leadership in how tools are deployed and leveraged

common_false_positives.behaviour: Universal adoption of core digital tools for planning and governance
common_false_positives.why_higher: Complete adoption feels like Optimised utilisation
common_false_positives.why_lower: Universal adoption of standard features is Integrated. Optimised requires that users innovate new use cases and drive continuous improvement beyond standard deployment

common_false_positives.behaviour: Regular tool upgrades are implemented for planning and governance
common_false_positives.why_higher: Staying current feels like optimisation
common_false_positives.why_lower: Upgrading is technology maintenance (Technology dimension). Optimised Utilisation means users actively drive new ways of working, not just accept upgrades

threshold_evidence.minimum: Evidence of user-driven innovation in tool use for planning and governance, continuous optimisation based on usage analytics, and sector recognition
threshold_evidence.strong: User-contributed innovations shared institution-wide, real-time analytics driving optimisation, quantified impact on planning and governance outcomes, peer recognition through case studies or visits
examples: Innovation showcase featuring user-created applications of planning and governance tools
Vendor or sector body case study on the institution's planning and governance tool utilisation
